name: Mitochondrial Disease with Epilepsy

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Mitochondrial Disease Diagnostic Criteria with Epilepsy Features

criteria.description: Presence of recurrent unprovoked seizures consistent with epilepsy
Evidence of mitochondrial respiratory chain enzyme deficiency in muscle biopsy or other tissues
Identification of pathogenic mitochondrial DNA or nuclear DNA mutations associated with mitochondrial disease
MRI findings suggestive of mitochondrial encephalopathy such as basal ganglia lesions or stroke-like episodes
Elevated lactate levels in blood or cerebrospinal fluid

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of clinical epilepsy plus biochemical evidence of mitochondrial dysfunction; genetic confirmation supports diagnosis but is not mandatory.
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis often requires multidisciplinary evaluation including neurology, genetics, and metabolic specialists.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Stroke-like episodes with transient neurological deficits

searchTerms: high lactic acid during metabolic crisis
muscle weakness and poor exercise tolerance

laboratory: Elevated blood and cerebrospinal fluid lactate and pyruvate
Muscle biopsy showing ragged-red fibers and cytochrome c oxidase deficiency
Elevated serum creatine kinase in some cases
imaging: MRI brain showing stroke-like lesions, basal ganglia abnormalities, and cerebral atrophy
Magnetic resonance spectroscopy demonstrating elevated lactate peaks
genetic: Pathogenic variants in mitochondrial DNA genes such as MT-TL1, MT-ND5
Nuclear gene mutations affecting mitochondrial function (e.g., POLG, TWNK)
other: Cardiac evaluation revealing cardiomyopathy or conduction abnormalities

distinguishingFeatures: Characteristic symmetric lesions in basal ganglia and brainstem on MRI
Different genetic mutations primarily in nuclear DNA

redFlags: Refractory seizures despite standard antiepileptic therapy
Progressive neurological deterioration with multisystem involvement
Episodes of metabolic decompensation with lactic acidosis
references: DiMauro S, Schon EA. Mitochondrial respiratory-chain diseases. N Engl J Med. 2003 Jun 19;348(26):2656-68.
Parikh S, Goldstein A, Karaa A, et al. Diagnosis and management of mitochondrial disease: a consensus statement from the Mitochondrial Medicine Society. Genet Med. 2015 Sep;17(9):689-701.
Finsterer J. Mitochondrial epilepsy. Epilepsy Res. 2008 Apr;78(2-3):121-37.
